idiom_name: hand-written class implementing the abstract repository interface over std::unordered_map
implementation_notes: The classic structure is written by hand: declare the collaborator as an abstract base class (or a virtual interface), then give the test a subclass that implements the same operations over std::unordered_map - no framework is involved, and gMock would generate a mock with expectations rather than a working fake. Prefer the fake when the tests need write-then-read sequences; the store is cheap because unordered_map gives average constant-time insertion and lookup. Construct the fake per test (or clear it) so no state leaks, and mark it final in tests to prevent accidental further derivation.
pitfalls: A missing override specifier hides a signature drift: the method becomes a new non-virtual overload and the SUT keeps calling the base's pure virtual (or the code only fails when the base changes).
A fake held by value in a fixture is copied or sliced when handed to the SUT; pass it through the interface by reference or pointer so both sides observe one stateful instance.
unordered_map is not thread-safe, and a fake shared between parallel test threads needs external synchronisation or a mutex member.
